usage: 건네다 is the verb for passing an object to someone right next to you.
Use 건네다 for the physical act of putting something in someone's hand.
examples: 친구에게 책을 건넸어요
I handed the book to my friend
Particle 에게 marks the person you hand it to.
저쪽 사람에게 메뉴판을 건네 주세요
Please hand the menu to that person
건네 주세요 softens it into a polite request.
그가 나에게 편지를 건넸어요
He handed me a letter
Everyday past-tense use of handing something over.
nuance: 건네다 means to pass or hand something directly to a person nearby, usually placing it in their hand. It is often used as 건네주다 (건네 주세요) when you ask someone to pass an item for you. Because the stem ends in the vowel ㅔ, 건네 + 어 simply contracts to 건네, so the polite form is 건네요, not 건네어요.
mistakes: Don't write the past as 건네었어요 — the ㅔ stem contracts, so it is 건넸어요.

usage: Please give back the book you borrowed
돌려주다 is the standard verb for returning a borrowed thing to its owner.
When will you give the money back?
Use it to ask about getting your money or things returned.
examples: 우산 내일 돌려줄게요
I'll give the umbrella back tomorrow
돌려줄게요 promises to return something later.
이거 누구한테 돌려줘야 해요?
Who do I have to give this back to?
한테 marks the person who should get it back.
친구가 돈을 돌려줬어요
My friend gave the money back
Past tense of returning money.
nuance: 돌려주다 literally combines 돌리다 (turn/return) + 주다 (give), so it means to give something back to the person it belongs to. It is the everyday word for returning borrowed items, money, or anything you took. Since it ends in 주다, all conjugations follow 주다: 돌려줘요, 돌려줬어요, 돌려주세요.
mistakes: Don't use 갚다 for returning objects — 갚다 is mainly for paying back money or debts, while 돌려주다 covers any borrowed thing.

english: to look after / pack for someone
usage: I make sure they eat well
챙겨주다 means caring for someone by getting their things or food ready.
Please pack/grab the umbrella for me
Use it to ask someone to get an item ready on your behalf.
examples: 엄마가 도시락을 챙겨줬어요
Mom packed a lunchbox for me
A warm, common use: a parent preparing things for you.
아이 준비물을 챙겨줘요
I get the kid's supplies ready
챙겨주다 for preparing someone else's belongings.
친구가 약을 챙겨줬어요
My friend got my medicine ready for me
Showing care by handling someone's needs.
nuance: 챙겨주다 (from 챙기다 + 주다) means to thoughtfully gather, pack, or take care of someone's things or needs for them. It carries a caring, looking-after feeling, so Koreans use it a lot about family and close friends. Like all 주다 verbs, it conjugates as 챙겨줘요, 챙겨줬어요, 챙겨주세요.
mistakes: Don't drop the 주 when you mean doing it for someone — 챙기다 alone means you pack for yourself, while 챙겨주다 means doing it for another person.

usage: 나르다 means moving heavy things from one place to another.
Use it when asking someone to haul an item somewhere.
examples: 물을 부엌으로 날랐어요
I carried the water to the kitchen
나르다 for moving things from place to place.
우리가 의자를 다 날랐어요
We carried all the chairs
Past tense 날랐어요 from the 르 irregular.
짐을 차까지 날라 줄까요?
Shall I carry the bags to the car for you?
Offering to haul something for someone.
nuance: 나르다 means to physically carry or haul objects (often heavy or many) from one spot to another, like luggage, boxes, or water. It is a 르-irregular verb: before 아/어 the 르 changes, so 나르 + 아 → 날라, giving 날라요 and 날랐어요. The future and can-forms keep the stem: 나를 거예요, 나를 수 있어요.
mistakes: Don't write 나르아요 — as a 르 irregular it becomes 날라요 with a doubled ㄹ.

usage: 가져다주다 means fetching something and bringing it to a person.
Casual everyday request to fetch an item.
examples: 엄마가 약을 가져다줬어요
Mom brought me the medicine
Someone fetching and delivering an item to you.
이 책 좀 동생에게 가져다줄래요?
Can you take this book to my sibling?
가져다주다 plus 에게 marks the receiver.
점원이 메뉴판을 가져다줬어요
The clerk brought the menu
Common in shops and restaurants.
nuance: 가져다주다 combines 가지다 (have/take) + 다 + 주다 (give), and means to go get something and bring it to someone. It is the natural verb for asking a server or family member to fetch and deliver an item. As a 주다 compound it conjugates as 가져다줘요, 가져다줬어요, 가져다주세요.
mistakes: Don't confuse it with 가져가다 (take away from here) — 가져다주다 brings the item TO someone, while 가져가다 carries it away.

english: to carry on one's shoulder / back
usage: I carry a bag (on my shoulder)
메다 is specifically for bags/straps worn on the shoulder or back.
메고 + verb describes doing something while carrying a bag.
examples: 책가방을 메고 학교에 가요
I go to school carrying my schoolbag
메고 shows the bag is worn while moving.
무거운 배낭을 멨어요
I carried a heavy backpack
Past tense 멨어요 from the ㅔ stem.
가방 한쪽으로 메지 마세요
Don't carry the bag on just one shoulder
Polite negative command with 메다.
nuance: 메다 means to carry something with a strap over your shoulder or on your back, like a backpack or bag. It is more specific than 들다 (to carry in the hand). Because the stem ends in ㅔ, 메 + 어 contracts to 메, so the polite form is 메요 and the past is 멨어요.
mistakes: Don't use 들다 for a backpack worn on the back — 들다 is carrying in the hand, while a shoulder/back bag uses 메다.

usage: I carry the baby on my back
업다 means piggybacking a person on your back.
I'm carrying the baby on my back
업고 있다 describes the ongoing state of piggybacking.
examples: 엄마가 아이를 업었어요
Mom carried the child on her back
A very common scene with small children.
할머니를 업고 갔어요
I carried grandma on my back
Used when helping someone who can't walk.
아기 업어 줄까요?
Shall I carry the baby on my back?
Offering to piggyback for someone.
nuance: 업다 means to carry a person (usually a baby or someone who can't walk) on your back, piggyback style. It is a regular consonant-stem verb, NOT a ㅂ-irregular, so it keeps the ㅂ: 업 + 어 → 업어요, past 업었어요, and the polite command 업으세요. Don't confuse it with 엎다 (to overturn).
mistakes: Don't treat 업다 as a ㅂ irregular — it stays regular, giving 업어요 (not 어워요).

usage: I load the luggage into the car
싣다 is for putting cargo onto a car, truck, or other vehicle.
I loaded everything into the trunk
Use it when placing things into a vehicle for transport.
examples: 상자를 트럭에 실었어요
I loaded the boxes onto the truck
싣다 with 에 marks the vehicle.
이거 차에 실어 주세요
Please load this into the car
Polite request to load an item.
짐이 많아서 다 실을 수 없어요
There's too much luggage to load it all
Can-form 실을 수 from the ㄷ irregular.
nuance: 싣다 means to load cargo or luggage onto a vehicle like a car or truck. It is a ㄷ-irregular verb: before a vowel the ㄷ changes to ㄹ, so 싣 + 어 → 실어요, past 실었어요, and 실을 거예요. Before a consonant the ㄷ stays: 싣고, 싣지, 싣습니다.
mistakes: Don't write 싣어요 — as a ㄷ irregular the ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, giving 실어요.

usage: 나눠주다 means dividing something and giving a share to each person.
Use it when passing one item each to many people.
examples: 선생님이 사탕을 나눠줬어요
The teacher handed out candy
A common classroom scene of handing out items.
이거 친구들한테 나눠줄까요?
Shall we hand these out to our friends?
나눠줄까요 suggests sharing them around.
음식을 사람들에게 나눠줬어요
I shared the food out to people
Dividing food and giving portions away.
nuance: 나눠주다 (from 나누다 share/divide + 주다 give) means to divide something up and hand a portion to each person. It implies giving to several people, like passing out snacks or handouts. As a 주다 compound it conjugates as 나눠줘요, 나눠줬어요, 나눠주세요.
mistakes: Don't use plain 나누다 when you mean handing portions to others — 나눠주다 adds the 'give to people' meaning that 나누다 alone lacks.

usage: 내밀다 means extending a body part or object out toward someone.
Use it when you stick something forward to show or hand it.
examples: 아이가 손을 내밀었어요
The child held out their hand
Common gesture, e.g. asking for something.
창밖으로 손을 내밀지 마세요
Don't stick your hand out the window
Polite negative command with 내밀다.
그가 명함을 내밀었어요
He held out his business card
Extending an object toward someone to hand it over.
nuance: 내밀다 means to push or extend something forward — often a hand, or an object you are presenting (a ticket, a card). It is a ㄹ-irregular verb: the ㄹ drops before ㅂ and ㅅ, so the formal form is 내밉니다 and the polite command is 내미세요. Before a vowel the ㄹ stays: 내밀어요, 내밀었어요.
mistakes: Don't write the polite command as 내밀으세요 — the ㄹ drops, so it is 내미세요.

usage: Please pass this to my friend
전해주다 means delivering an item or message to someone for you.
Very common for sending greetings through a third person.
examples: 이 편지를 엄마에게 전해줬어요
I delivered this letter to mom
전해주다 with 에게 marks the receiver.
선물 좀 전해줄래요?
Could you pass on this gift?
Asking someone to deliver a gift for you.
사장님께 메시지를 전해줬어요
I passed the message to the boss
Used for relaying messages as well as objects.
nuance: 전해주다 (전하다 convey + 주다 give) means to pass an item or message on to someone, often through a third person. It works for physical things (a letter, a gift) and for messages or greetings (안부 전해줘요). As a 주다 compound it conjugates as 전해줘요, 전해줬어요, 전해주세요.
mistakes: Don't use 보내다 when handing something to a person directly — 보내다 is for sending at a distance, while 전해주다 is delivering it to them (often in person).
